1359.unvetted: Abhilekh Patal retested from the cloud on 11 Nov 2026: record HTTP 200 and the document viewer opened without a login, so the 49-page file (NAIDLF03824535) was read. Ciphertext is there: two long telegrams Nanking -> 'Dalai Buddha, Lhasa' in four-digit groups (pp. 14-15, about 155 and 75 groups; groups such as 0022 1135 2398 1650 look like the public Chinese Telegraph Code, i.e. readable from the code book, not tested further), and five telegrams from the Dalai Lama / Lhasa in ten-letter code words (p. 9 to Singchi c/o Thinyik Calcutta, 17 groups; pp. 11-12 to Chiang Kai-shek and Ma Fu-hsiang, 22 Sept 1930, about 25 and 20 groups; pp. 22-23 to Ma Fu-hsiang and Yoong Kun Dzasa, 13 Oct 1930, about 34 groups each). No decipherment is written on them, but the file shows the traffic was read: the Foreign and Political Dept sent Weir 'an abstract of some messages' (D.O. 29 Sept 1930, p. 18) and further notes (14 Oct 1930, Jan 1931), and from Jan 1931 the General Staff Branch, Simla (Major Ruck) sent 'burn after reading' summaries. Missing: the General Staff decrypts themselves (not in this file; look in IOR L/P&S/12 Tibet files and NAI General Staff Branch), which is a parallel decipherment series not opened. Three web searches and DECODE (Dalai, Lhasa, Tibet, Nanking: 0 records) found no published text. If kept, recast the lead as the Dalai Lama's letter-code telegrams of Sept-Oct 1930.
